claims.text: Applying a controlled nanoscale surface treatment to a high-entropy alloy will reduce its coefficient of friction relative to the untreated alloy.
Applying the surface treatment will reduce the high-entropy alloy's wear rate relative to the untreated alloy.
The reductions in friction and wear will persist over a broad service-temperature range extending from room temperature to approximately 800 °C.
A deposition method such as plasma spraying can provide the proposed controlled nanoscale surface treatment.
The engineered surface layer will catalyze formation of an ultra-thin tribo-oxide film during sliding.
Sliding and thermal stress will cause the treated surface to react with the environment and form a lubricious oxide layer.
The tribo-oxide layer will adapt to different temperatures and sliding loads.
The tribo-oxide layer will reduce friction and wear through surface passivation and lubrication.
Untreated high-entropy alloys exhibit higher and more temperature-sensitive friction and wear than the proposed treated alloys.
The treatment should remain effective during dynamic loading and temperature fluctuations typical of moving components.
Extreme mechanical overload or operation beyond the engineered temperature range may limit the treatment's performance.
